newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine revises down 97 grain harvest forecast.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine revises down 97 grain harvest forecast.

text.p: Ukraine's agriculture minister revised down on Thursday his 1997 grain harvest forecast to 35 million tonnes from 39.1 million tonnes and said exports this year would total 10 million tonnes.
"We plan a larger harvest than last year -- 35 million tonnes," Mykhailo Zubets told a news conference. "As for exports, there would be 10 million tonnes."
"Last year, I said we would export 3 to 5 million tonnes of grain. We sold more," he added.

The Agriculture Ministry forecast on Wednesday a harvest of 39.1 million tonnes, including a winter wheat crop of 20.8 million tonnes, compared to 13.4 million tonnes of winter wheat harvested last year. Last year's harvest was a poor 25.4 million tonnes.

"Last year, we sowed significantly more winter grain, and today thanks be to God or to the weather it is in much better shape this year than last year," Zubets, appointed by President Leonid Kuchma this week, said.

Zubets, also Deputy Prime Minister in charge of agriculture, said the sector still faced many problems, such as shortages of fuel, seed, herbicides, and machinery. "But we have received 1.5 billion hryvnias from the government in material and technical resources, which is three times more than last year," he said.
The ministry has forecast total sowing for all spring crops at 15.18 million hectares against 14.55 million hectares last year.
"If our spring sowing is successful and we can increase our spring grain crop, we can reverse the drop of recent years and increase our grain production this year," Zubets said.
Last year's grain crop, the lowest in decades, was blamed on a drought at the start of the growing season.
